title: POC scoping - Kepler Solutions integration planning
summary: Kickoff POC scoping focused on integration approach: SDKs vs OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, structured outputs. Covered success criteria (latency, cost, quality thresholds), workload sizing for demo traffic, benchmark plan, and a 4-week timeline with checkpoints. Security and data residency questions noted.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-12
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Kepler Eng Lead), Maya Patel (Kepler PM), Samir Khan (Kepler Security)
---
00:00 Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining. we're excited to scope this poc with Kepler. quick intros?
00:08 Tom: hey Tom here, engineering lead. Maya product, Samir security. thanks.
00:13 Priya: hi all, priya, i'll be the SE ill dig into integrations and perf.
00:18 Maya: great. main goal today is alignment on success criteria and the integration approach, right?
00:24 Alex: yep. high level we want to make sure we can hit latency and cost targets and validate function calling for structured outputs.
00:30 Tom: cool. current stack: microservices on k8s in GCP, we use Vertex for batch ML and some in-house heuristics. we want to replace/reroute a subset of inference to Redwood hosted initially.
00:42 Priya: ok, and do you expect to use Redwood hosted or private (VPC) for this POC?
00:47 Maya: for POC hosted is fine but we need KMS integration for logs. production may move to private.
00:53 Samir: and SOC2 requirements, audit logs, SSO, RBAC, encryption, basically enterprise controls will be evaluating.
01:01 Alex: noted. success criteria question what are your target SLOs?
01:06 Tom: 95th percentile latency under 350 ms for single-turn prompts, and overall cost per 1k tokens under $0.80 equivalent. Quality: top-line accuracy vs our current classifier > +10% on our labeled set.
01:22 Priya: good measurable goals. for latency we need to know sequence lengths, tokens per request, and concurrency. can you share typical prompt lengths?
01:30 Tom: most requests are between 30 and 180 tokens, median 60. concurrency during peak 100 RPS targeting for the demo; sustained 20 RPS baseline.
01:40 Priya: got it so we'll plan benchmarks at three load profiles: low (20 RPS), peak (100 RPS), and spike (200 RPS burst).
01:48 Maya: what's Redwood's recommended integration? we prefer to use our existing OpenAI-compatible clients if possible.
01:53 Priya: you can use either our official SDKs (python/node) which offer seamless batching, caching, and structured output helpers, or our OpenAI-compatible endpoint. the endpoint supports function calling and streaming. small caveat: some advanced batching features are only available via the SDK not an API showstopper but helpful for cost.
02:10 Tom: is function calling compatible when using the OpenAI-compatible endpoint?
02:14 Priya: yes we do occasionally see docs where the name is slightly different; some transcriptions say "tool calling" but it's the same. structured outputs: we can enforce JSON schema and run post-checks.
02:25 Samir: about data: what goes to logs and how long is retained?
02:29 Alex: by default hosted retains minimal logs; for POC we'll set retention to 30 days. For production with Private you can keep logs in your VPC and integrate KMS/HSM; Samir, we have SOC2 docs and an audit pack we can share.
02:41 Maya: timeline what's realistic to run benchmarks and have artifacts?
02:45 Alex: propose 4-week POC: week1 integration & ingest sample data, week2 baseline benchmarks, week3 optimize batching/quantization suggestions, week4 run final benchmarks and review.
02:56 Tom: sounds good. what about endpoints do you want to demo SDK quickstart?
03:00 Priya: yes, we'll send a quickstart repo. for your engineers we recommend using the SDK for initial runs, then switch to OpenAI-compatible endpoint if you want to replace clients quickly.
03:10 Tom: on throughput what hardware will be backing hosted? any guarantees?
03:14 Alex: for hosted POC we'll route to Redwood shared capacity; we'll provide expected perf profiles by model. dedicated capacity (reserved) is an option if you need predictable throughput that comes later.
03:25 Maya: benchmark specifics what metrics will Redwood capture?
03:28 Priya: per-request latency (p50/p90/p95), token throughput, cost per 1k tokens, error rates, and model output diffs vs your golden set. we'll give raw traces and per-route breakdowns in the console.
03:39 Tom: can we run an A/B comparing your model vs our current classifier?
03:42 Priya: yes can do A/B and canary. we'll produce a benchmark spreadsheet template; will need labeled test set and evaluation prompts.
03:51 Samir: security will PII be sent? mostly non-PII but some customer strings could be sensitive.
03:57 Alex: recommend redaction prior to POC or use Private with customer-managed encryption. we also support field-level redaction in SDK to avoid sending raw PII.
04:08 Maya: integration concerns: we rely heavily on function calling to get structured JSON outputs that map to our data model. can Redwood enforce JSON schema?
04:15 Priya: yes we support structured output enforcement; we validate and can fallback to deterministic parsing. note sometimes generative models hallucinate field names we'll run a validation step and add sampling/penalty tuning.
04:29 Tom: any SDK examples for function calling?
04:32 Priya: i'll drop a sample in the quickstart. it uses the SDK's call_function helper which wraps OpenAI-style function calls and returns a deterministic JSON blob; it also handles streaming partials.
04:44 Tom: okay. benchmarks how do we simulate concurrency from our side?
04:48 Priya: we can provide a load script using our perf harness or you can run JMeter/Locust hitting the OpenAI-compatible endpoint; we'll share recommended traffic patterns and warm-up sequences to populate KV cache.
04:59 Maya: what's KV cache? I heard it earlier as "KV cash" on another call.
05:03 Priya: (laughs) it's KV cache key-value cache for prefix tokens, used to reduce per-token compute for repeated contexts. important for chat workloads.
05:12 Tom: ok, for the POC we'll provide: sample payloads, labeled eval set, and a small traffic replay.
05:18 Alex: perfect. we'll outline an experiment plan: define benchmarks, share spreadsheet, run baseline runs with your traffic, and then optimization passes.
05:28 Maya: any blockers on legal/privacy? Samir?
05:31 Samir: we'll need the security pack and data flows. also SSO for console access and least privileged roles.
05:36 Alex: we'll share SOC2, ISO summary, support SSO via SAML, and you can map RBAC roles.
05:44 Tom: question on model selection what models do you recommend for short prompts vs long context?
05:48 Priya: for short prompts we suggest the low-latency family (redwood-rt*), for longer context we can use models with longer context windows. exact names in the catalog, note some names get munged in transcripts.
05:58 Tom: do we need to worry about quantization or accuracy loss?
06:02 Priya: we'll propose quantization profiles after initial runs; often 4-bit quantization gives big cost wins with minor quality drop, but we'll measure against your eval metrics.
06:12 Maya: finalize timeline and next steps?
06:14 Alex: propose: today alignment. by Tue (2026-05-14) we'll send quickstart repo, benchmark spreadsheet, and security pack. Week of 5/18 you'll run integration and provide sample traffic. Week of 5/25 we'll run baseline benchmarks. Week of 6/1 optimization pass. Final review week of 6/8.
06:34 Tom: that works.
06:36 Priya: action items we'll capture but also send calendar invites for checkpoints.
06:40 Maya: any competitors mentioned? we did an initial eval vs OpenAI and Vertex internally.
06:45 Alex: ok noted.
06:48 Tom: small nit, when you said "OpenAI-compatible" earlier we want it to be drop-in for our existing clients.
06:52 Priya: yes it's compatible; for streaming and function calling semantics we maintain parity but recommend SDK for batching and KV cache management.
06:59 Samir: one more security ask can we run a quick pen-test before ramp?
07:03 Alex: yes, we support that in Private and enterprise plans; for hosted we can do a scope-limited assessment.
07:10 Maya: great. let's recap next steps.
07:13 Alex: recap: 1) Redwood sends quickstart, benchmark sheet, security pack by 2026-05-14. 2) Kepler to provide sample traffic, labeled eval set by 2026-05-18. 3) Redwood runs baseline benchmarks week of 2026-05-25. 4) Optimization pass week of 2026-06-01. 5) Final review week of 2026-06-08.
07:35 Tom: cool. thanks everyone.
07:38 Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.
07:41 END

Notes on transcription: Some words may be slightly off (e.g., "KV cash", "Redwood Deicated"), filler words removed in places, occasional speaker mis-attribution (auto-attrib had Maya/Mark confused early).
